title: How many flowers go through the three magical ponds?
description: Flowers double in each of three magical ponds, and the same number is placed in each of three shrines. Letters for the start and for the flowers in each shrine give eight ex equals seven kay, so seven flowers and eight in each shrine work, and so do their multiples.
teaching_notes: One idea: follow the flowers through each pond and shrine with two letters, then the last shrine gives the equation. Watch for students who write only one answer and miss that every multiple also works.

video_script.why: The child uses the double and take away working from the solved sticker puzzle, now with three rounds and two unknown letters.
video_script.substitution: Let x be the start and k the flowers in each shrine, follow three ponds to 8x − 6k = k, so 8x = 7k, take x = 7 and k = 8, and check.
video_script.anchor: three ponds and three shrines in a row, flowers doubling at each pond and a heap placed at each shrine
video_script.payoff_line: The person started with seven flowers and places eight in each shrine, or any multiple of these

final_answer.value: 7 flowers at the start, 8 in each shrine
final_answer.spoken: seven flowers at the start and eight in each shrine

maths_rules: let x be the start and k the flowers in each shrine
after pond 1 and shrine 1: 2x − k; after pond 2 and shrine 2: 2 (2x − k) − k = 4x − 3k
pond 3 doubles it to 8x − 6k, and all of it goes into shrine 3, so 8x − 6k = k and 8x = 7k
smallest whole numbers: x = 7 and k = 8; any multiple, such as 14 and 16, also works
video_script.design: One idea: two letters follow the flowers through three ponds, and the last shrine gives the equation. The row of ponds and shrines stays on the board and the check is the last step.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book. Three shrines each have a magical pond in front.
<bookmark mark='pond'/>Flowers dipped in a pond double in number. A person dips all the flowers in the first pond, then places some in shrine one.
<bookmark mark='rounds'/>The remaining flowers go into the second pond. Some are placed in shrine two.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The rest go into the third pond. All of them are placed in shrine three.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The same number goes in each shrine. How many flowers did the person start with, and how many go in each shrine?

beats.on_screen: the ponds and shrines stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: pond = times 2; shrine = take away k; letters x and k

marks.plan: the pond is marked as times 2 and the shrine as take away

narration: <bookmark mark='plan'/>We follow the flowers with letters, as in the sticker puzzle. A pond means times two, and a shrine means taking flowers away.

beats.on_screen: Given: 3 ponds, 3 shrines, the same number of flowers in each shrine

marks.given: the three ponds and three shrines are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, three ponds and three shrines, with the same number of flowers placed in each shrine.

beats.on_screen: To find: the flowers at the start, and the flowers in each shrine

marks.find: the two aims are written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the flowers at the start, and the flowers in each shrine.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: let x = flowers at the start; k = flowers in each shrine

marks.let: x and k are written with their meanings

beats.colours: x and k in two colours
narration: <bookmark mark='let'/>Step one, let ex be the flowers at the start, and kay the flowers in each shrine.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: after shrine 1: 2x − k; after shrine 2: 2 (2x − k) − k = 4x − 3k

marks.one: 2x − k is written for the first pond and shrine
marks.two: 2 (2x − k) − k = 4x − 3k is written for the second

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step two, follow the first two ponds. After the first pond and shrine we have two ex take away kay.
<bookmark mark='two'/>After the second, we double that and take away kay, which is four ex take away three kay.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: pond 3 gives 8x − 6k, and all of it is k; so 8x − 6k = k and 8x = 7k

marks.three: 8x − 6k is written for the third pond
marks.add: 6k is added to both sides to give 8x = 7k

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, the third pond doubles what is left, which is eight ex take away six kay.
<bookmark mark='eq'/>All of it goes into shrine three, so it is equal to kay.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Add six kay to both sides, and eight ex is seven kay.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: 8x = 7k gives x = 7 and k = 8; any multiple, like 14 and 16, also works

marks.more: 14 and 16 are written as another pair that works

narration: <bookmark mark='small'/>Step four, take the smallest whole numbers that fit. Ex is seven and kay is eight.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Any multiple of these also works, such as fourteen and sixteen.

marks.three: 4 × 2 = 8 is written and matched with k

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step five, check with seven. Seven doubled is fourteen, and fourteen take away eight is six.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Six doubled is twelve, and twelve take away eight is four.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Four doubled is eight, the same as kay.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 7 flowers and 8 in each shrine (or any multiple, like 14 and 16)

marks.ans: the answer 7 flowers and 8 in each shrine is boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The person started with seven flowers and places eight in each shrine, or any multiple of these.
